# Setup

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)
```

## Required Packages

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(microseq)
library(Rsearch)
```

## Global Settings

```{r}
setwd("/path/to/working/directory") # Path to your working directory
```

## Prepare Directories and Paths

```{r}
path                <- "10000_species_10_dynamic"         # Define the dataset to process
fastq.folder        <- file.path(path, "fastq")           # Directory containing the raw FASTQ files
fastq_filt.folder   <- file.path(path, "fastq_filtered")  # Directory containing quality-filtered FASTQ files
fasta_merged.folder <- file.path(path, "fasta_merged")    # Directory containing merged FASTA files
rsearch_dir         <- file.path(path, "rsearch_results") # Directory containing Rsearch output
fasta.folder        <- file.path(rsearch_dir, "fasta")    # Directory containing dereplicated FASTA files
metadata.file       <- file.path(path, "metadata.tsv")    # Path to the metadata file

swarm_results_folder <- file.path(path, "swarm_results") # Directory containing Swarm clustering output
```

## Metadata

```{r}
load(file.path(rsearch_dir, "metadata.tbl.RData"))  # Load the metadata table produced by the Rsearch pipeline
```

# Swarm Results Processing

```{r}
for (i in 1:nrow(metadata.tbl)) {                                                 # Iterate over each sample in the metadata table
  
  message(paste0("Processing sample ", 
                 metadata.tbl$sample_id[i], 
                 " (", i, "/", nrow(metadata.tbl), ")"))
  
  # ---------------------------
  # Load and parse input data
  # ---------------------------
  
  all.tbl <- readFasta(file.path(fasta.folder, 
                                 metadata.tbl$dereplicated_fasta[i])) %>%         # Read the dereplicated FASTA file for the current sample
    mutate(actual_cluster = Header,
           actual_cluster = str_match(actual_cluster,
                                      "tax=(.*)_[0-9]+_[0-9]+/[0-9]+;")[,2]) %>%  # Extract the taxonomic label from the FASTA header as the ground truth cluster identity
    mutate(size = str_extract(Header, "(?<=;size=)\\d+") %>%                      # Parse the dereplicated sequence size (read count) from the FASTA header
             as.numeric()
    )
  
  metadata.tbl$n_species_pre_clustering[i] <- 
    length(unique(all.tbl$actual_cluster))                                        # Record the number of distinct species present after dereplication
  
  # Read swarm output file
  swarm.tbl <- read_tsv(
    file.path(path, "swarm_results", 
              paste0(metadata.tbl$sample_id[i], "_dereplicated_swarm.uc")),
    col_names = c("record_type", "cluster_number", 
                  "length_size", "percent_similarity", 
                  "match_orientation", "X6", "X7", 
                  "X8", "X9", "X10"))                                             # Read the SWARM UC-format output file for the current sample
  
  c.tbl <- swarm.tbl %>% 
    rename(Header = X9,
           centroid = X10) %>%                                                    # Rename positional UC columns to meaningful names
    select(-c("length_size", "match_orientation", "X6", "X7", 
              "X8")) %>%                                                          # Drop columns not needed for downstream analysis
    filter(record_type != "C") %>% 
    mutate(size = str_extract(Header, "(?<=;size=)\\d+")) %>%                     # Remove cluster summary rows; retain only seed (S) and hit (H) records
    mutate(size = as.numeric(size)) %>%                                           # Parse the sequence size from the header
    mutate(cluster_number = as.character(cluster_number)) %>% 
    mutate(centroid = ifelse(centroid == "*", Header, centroid))                  # Replace the placeholder "*" with the sequence's own header for centroid records
  
  # ---------------------------
  # Filter singleton clusters
  # ---------------------------
  
  c_modified.tbl <- c.tbl %>%
    group_by(cluster_number) %>%
    filter(!(n() == 1 & record_type == "S" & size == 1)) %>%
    ungroup()                                                                     # Remove clusters consisting of a single centroid sequence with only one read
  
  metadata.tbl$n_clusters[i] <- length(unique(c_modified.tbl$cluster_number))     # Record the number of clusters remaining after singleton removal
  
  res.tbl <- c_modified.tbl %>%
    arrange(cluster_number) %>% 
    mutate(predicted_cluster = centroid,
           predicted_cluster = str_match(
             predicted_cluster, "tax=(.*)_[0-9]+_[0-9]+/[0-9]+;")[,2]) %>%        # Extract the taxonomic label of the cluster centroid as the predicted cluster identity
    mutate(actual_cluster = Header,
           actual_cluster = str_match(
             actual_cluster, "tax=(.*)_[0-9]+_[0-9]+/[0-9]+;")[,2]) %>%           # Extract the taxonomic label of each member sequence as the ground truth identity
    left_join(all.tbl %>% select(Header, Sequence), by = "Header")                # Attach the nucleotide sequence for each cluster member
  
  # ---------------
  # Purity analysis
  # ---------------
  
  # Prepare the data
  clustering_results.tbl <- res.tbl                                               # Alias for readability in the purity analysis section
  
  cluster_summary <- clustering_results.tbl %>%
    filter(!is.na(cluster_number)) %>%
    group_by(cluster_number) %>%
    summarise(
      total_reads = sum(size),
      distinct_actual_clusters = 
        n_distinct(actual_cluster),                                               # Count the number of distinct ground truth species within each predicted cluster
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(status = ifelse(           
      distinct_actual_clusters == 1,
      "Pure",
      "Mixed")
    ) %>%                                                                         # Classify each cluster as pure (single species) or mixed (multiple species)
    arrange(status, desc(total_reads))                                            # Sort so mixed clusters appear first, then by descending read count
  
  
  metadata.tbl$n_pure_clusters[i] <- sum(cluster_summary$status == "Pure")        # Record the number of pure clusters for this sample
  
  purity_summary <- clustering_results.tbl %>%
    filter(!is.na(cluster_number)) %>%
    group_by(cluster_number, actual_cluster) %>%
    summarise(size_per_group = sum(size), .groups = "drop_last") %>%              # Sum read counts for each species within each predicted cluster
    arrange(desc(size_per_group)) %>%
    summarise(
      total_cluster_size = sum(size_per_group),                                   # Total number of reads assigned to this predicted cluster
      dominant_actual = first(actual_cluster),                                    # The species contributing the most reads to this cluster
      dominant_size = first(size_per_group),                                      # Read count of the dominant species in this cluster
      purity_pct = dominant_size / total_cluster_size                             # Cluster purity: proportion of reads belonging to the dominant species
    ) %>%
    arrange(purity_pct)
  
  total_reads <- clustering_results.tbl %>%
    filter(!is.na(cluster_number)) %>% 
    select(size) %>% 
    sum()                                                                         # Calculate the total number of reads across all clusters for normalization
  
  metadata.tbl$average_purity_score[i] <- mean(purity_summary$purity_pct)         # Average per-cluster purity across all clusters in this sample
  
  # -------------------------
  # Perfect clusters analysis
  #--------------------------
  
  input_totals <- all.tbl %>%
    group_by(actual_cluster) %>%
    summarise(total_size_in = sum(size, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")          # Calculate the total read count per species in the input before clustering
  
  cluster_summary <- clustering_results.tbl %>%
    group_by(cluster_number) %>%
    summarise(
      n_species_in_cluster = n_distinct(actual_cluster),                          # Count the number of distinct species present in each cluster
      cluster_species = first(actual_cluster),                                    # Record the species name (meaningful only for single-species clusters)
      total_size_out = sum(size, na.rm = TRUE),                                   # Total number of reads in each cluster after clustering
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  species_distribution <- clustering_results.tbl %>%
    group_by(actual_cluster) %>%
    summarise(n_groups_for_species = n_distinct(cluster_number, na.rm = FALSE),   # Count how many predicted clusters each species is distributed across
              .groups = "drop")
  
  perfect_clusters <- cluster_summary %>%
    filter(!is.na(cluster_number)) %>%
    filter(n_species_in_cluster == 1) %>%                                         # Retain only single-species clusters
    left_join(species_distribution, 
              by = c("cluster_species" = "actual_cluster")) %>%
    filter(n_groups_for_species == 1) %>%                                         # Retain only species that appear in exactly one cluster
    left_join(input_totals, by = c("cluster_species" = "actual_cluster")) %>%
    filter(total_size_out == total_size_in)                                       # Retain only clusters where all reads for the species are recovered (no read loss)
  
  metadata.tbl$n_perfect_clusters[i] <- nrow(perfect_clusters)                    # Record the number of perfect clusters: pure, non-split, and complete
  
  
  # ------------------------------------------
  # Represented species and abundance profiles
  #-------------------------------------------
  
  dominant_species_per_cluster <- clustering_results.tbl %>%
    filter(!is.na(cluster_number)) %>%
    group_by(cluster_number, actual_cluster) %>%
    summarise(total_size = sum(size), .groups = "drop_last") %>%
    arrange(cluster_number, desc(total_size)) %>%
    summarise(dominant_actual_cluster = first(actual_cluster), 
              .groups = "drop")                                                   # Assign each predicted cluster to the species contributing the most reads
  
  metadata.tbl$n_species_represented[i] <- 
    length(unique(dominant_species_per_cluster$dominant_actual_cluster))          # Record the number of distinct species represented by at least one cluster
  
  n_species_with_multiple_clusters <- dominant_species_per_cluster %>%
    group_by(dominant_actual_cluster) %>%
    summarise(n_clusters = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(n_clusters >= 2) %>%
    nrow()                                                                        # Count species that dominate more than one predicted cluster (over-splitting)
  
  metadata.tbl$n_species_with_multiple_clusters[i] <- 
    n_species_with_multiple_clusters                                              # Record the number of over-split species for this sample
  
  fq <- readFastq(file.path(fastq.folder, metadata.tbl$R1_file[i])) %>%
    mutate(actual_cluster = Header,
           actual_cluster = str_match(
             actual_cluster, "tax=(.*)_[0-9]+_[0-9]+/[0-9]")[,2])                 # Read the R1 FASTQ file and extract the ground truth species label from each read header
  
  abundance_per_initiate_species <- fq %>%
    group_by(actual_cluster) %>%
    summarise(gold_standard_n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(gold_standard_rel_abundance = 
             gold_standard_n / sum(gold_standard_n)) %>%
    arrange(desc(gold_standard_rel_abundance))                                    # Calculate the ground truth relative abundance of each species from raw read counts
  
  abundance_per_species <- clustering_results.tbl %>%
    left_join(dominant_species_per_cluster, by = "cluster_number") %>% 
    mutate(dominant_actual_cluster = 
             replace_na(dominant_actual_cluster, "Unassigned")) %>%
    group_by(dominant_actual_cluster) %>%
    summarise(n = sum(size), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(rel_abundance = n / sum(n)) %>%
    arrange(desc(rel_abundance)) %>%
    rename(actual_cluster = dominant_actual_cluster)                              # Calculate the observed relative abundance of each species from clustering results
  
  abundance.tbl <- abundance_per_initiate_species %>%
    left_join(abundance_per_species, by = "actual_cluster") %>%
    mutate(n = replace_na(n, 0),
           rel_abundance = replace_na(rel_abundance, 0))                          # Combine ground truth and observed abundance tables; fill missing species with zero abundance
  
  metadata.tbl$abundance_correlation[i] <- cor(
    abundance.tbl$gold_standard_rel_abundance, 
    abundance.tbl$rel_abundance)                                                  # Calculate Pearson correlation between ground truth and observed relative abundances
  
  # ------------------------------------------
  # Non-clustered sequence statistics
  # ------------------------------------------
  
  nc.tbl <- c.tbl %>%
    group_by(cluster_number) %>%
    filter((n() == 1 & record_type == "S" & size == 1)) %>%                       # Isolate singleton clusters that were removed earlier (single seed with one read)
    ungroup() %>% 
    mutate(taxonomy = str_match(Header, 
                                "tax=(.*)_[0-9]+_[0-9]+/[0-9]")[,2]) %>%          # Extract the ground truth species label for each non-clustered sequence
    left_join(abundance_per_initiate_species, 
              by = c("taxonomy" = "actual_cluster"))                              # Attach ground truth abundance information for each non-clustered species
  
  metadata.tbl$n_reads_not_clustered[i] <- sum(nc.tbl$size)                       # Record the total number of reads that were not assigned to any cluster
  metadata.tbl$n_species_not_clustered[i] <- n_distinct(nc.tbl$taxonomy)          # Record the number of distinct species represented only by non-clustered sequences
  metadata.tbl$median_ground_truth_abundance[i] <- 
    median(nc.tbl$gold_standard_rel_abundance)                                    # Record the median ground truth abundance of species that failed to cluster
}

save(metadata.tbl, file = file.path(swarm_results_folder, "metadata.tbl.RData"))  # Save the updated metadata table with all collected statistics
```

## Plotting preperations

```{r}
# Load per-dataset metadata tables
load("path/to/some/directory/100_species_10_dynamic/swarm_results/metadata.tbl.RData")
metadata_100s_10d.tbl <- metadata.tbl    # 100 species, dynamic range 10

load("path/to/some/directory/100_species_100_dynamic/swarm_results/metadata.tbl.RData")
metadata_100s_100d.tbl <- metadata.tbl   # 100 species, dynamic range 100

load("path/to/some/directory/500_species_10_dynamic/swarm_results/metadata.tbl.RData")
metadata_500s_10d.tbl <- metadata.tbl    # 500 species, dynamic range 10

load("path/to/some/directory/500_species_100_dynamic/swarm_results/metadata.tbl.RData")
metadata_500s_100d.tbl <- metadata.tbl   # 500 species, dynamic range 100

load("path/to/some/directory/1000_species_10_dynamic/swarm_results/metadata.tbl.RData")
metadata_1000s_10d.tbl <- metadata.tbl   # 1000 species, dynamic range 10

load("path/to/some/directory/1000_species_100_dynamic/swarm_results/metadata.tbl.RData")
metadata_1000s_100d.tbl <- metadata.tbl  # 1000 species, dynamic range 100

load("path/to/some/directory/10000_species_10_dynamic/swarm_results/metadata.tbl.RData")
metadata_10000s_10d.tbl <- metadata.tbl  # 10000 species, dynamic range 10

load("path/to/some/directory/10000_species_100_dynamic/swarm_results/metadata.tbl.RData")
metadata_10000s_100d.tbl <- metadata.tbl # 10000 species, dynamic range 100

# Combine metadata tables by species richness
metadata_100s   <- bind_rows(metadata_100s_10d.tbl,   metadata_100s_100d.tbl)    # All 100-species datasets
metadata_500s   <- bind_rows(metadata_500s_10d.tbl,   metadata_500s_100d.tbl)    # All 500-species datasets
metadata_1000s  <- bind_rows(metadata_1000s_10d.tbl,  metadata_1000s_100d.tbl)   # All 1000-species datasets
metadata_10000s <- bind_rows(metadata_10000s_10d.tbl, metadata_10000s_100d.tbl)  # All 10000-species datasets

# Combine all datasets into a single table and label the pipeline
metadata_swarm_all.tbl <- bind_rows(metadata_100s, metadata_500s,
                                    metadata_1000s, metadata_10000s) %>%
  mutate(pipeline = "swarm")                                                      # Add a pipeline identifier column for downstream comparisons across methods

save(metadata_swarm_all.tbl, 
     file = "path/to/some/directory/metadata_all_swarm_tbl.RData")                # Save the combined metadata table for use in plotting
```
